note: Collected from public uta.edu pages on the collected date. 'verified' means every shown field was read on the cited official page; fields the page did not publish say so. Re-check before release (risk R-03, owner Krisha Patel).

Money & aid.name: Student Accounts
Money & aid.description: Handles tuition and fee billing, payment plans, account balances, refunds of credit balances and 1098-T questions. In-person service is on the first floor of the University Administration Building.
Money & aid.contact: Phone and email listed on the official Student Accounts page
next_steps: Review your balance and due dates in MyMav under Accounts.
Enroll in a payment plan before the posted deadline if you cannot pay in full.
Visit the office on the 1st floor of the University Administration Building for help with a specific charge.

Money & aid.name: Financial Aid & Scholarships
Money & aid.description: The Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships helps with the FAFSA and TASFA, grants, federal loans, work-study, TEXAS Grant and award packages. Walk-in service is available during business hours with no appointment.
Money & aid.hours: Mon–Fri, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. (in person, no appointment necessary)
next_steps: Submit or correct your FAFSA (or TASFA) using UTA's school code.
Check your aid status and outstanding requirements in MyMav.
Email fao@uta.edu with your UTA ID, or walk in to UAB B17.

Money & aid.name: Scholarship Support
Money & aid.description: The Scholarships Office manages UTA scholarship applications, renewals and award questions for incoming and continuing students.
next_steps: Review open scholarships and deadlines on the Scholarships page.
Complete the scholarship application before the priority deadline.
Email schol@uta.edu with your UTA ID for award questions.

Money & aid.name: Student Money Management
Money & aid.description: Financial-literacy help for budgeting, managing student loan debt and planning how to pay for college, offered through the Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships.
next_steps: Ask a financial aid counselor about budgeting and loan-management resources.
Review your total cost of attendance and loan balances before borrowing more.
Use campus food and emergency resources if a short-term shortfall threatens your enrollment.

Money & aid.name: Emergency Financial Assistance
Money & aid.description: The Emergency Assistance Fund, run by the Dean of Students, gives a one-time grant to enrolled students facing a sudden emergency such as eviction, fire, theft, a natural disaster, urgent safety needs or medical costs. It does not cover tuition.
Money & aid.location: Dean of Students, Continuing Education and Workforce Development Building, 140 W Mitchell St, Suite D100
next_steps: Apply online for the Emergency Assistance Fund.
Gather documentation such as photos, bills, an insurance claim or a doctor's note.
Watch your UTA email; the committee may contact you before a decision.

Money & aid.name: Veteran Education Benefits
Money & aid.description: The Military and Veterans Services Center certifies VA education benefits (GI Bill, Hazlewood and dependent benefits) and supports military-connected students.
Money & aid.location: Military and Veterans Services Center, 406 Summit Ave.
next_steps: Submit your VA certification request each semester after you register.
Bring your Certificate of Eligibility or Hazlewood paperwork.
Contact va@uta.edu or visit 406 Summit Ave.

Academics.name: University Advising
Academics.description: The University Advising Center advises first-year and undecided students on course selection, degree planning and choosing or changing a major. Drop-in advising is first come, first served.
Academics.hours: Mon–Thu, 8:30 a.m.–12:00 p.m. and 1:00–4:00 p.m. (Tue from 10:00 a.m.)
next_steps: Schedule an advising appointment online or drop in to Ransom Hall 100.
Bring your degree audit and a list of courses you are considering.
Ask your advisor to lift any advising hold before registration opens.

Academics.name: Tutoring & Academic Success
Academics.description: The Academic Success Center offers free tutoring, academic coaching and course support for many lower-level courses, including chemistry, biology and physics.
Academics.hours: Varies by program; see the course-support schedule
next_steps: Check which courses have tutoring this semester.
Visit Central Library 415 or Ransom Hall 206 during scheduled hours.
Book academic coaching if you need help with study habits or time management.

Academics.name: Writing Center
Academics.description: The English Writing Center gives one-on-one consultations at any stage of writing, from brainstorming to revising essays, research papers and application statements, including support for multilingual writers.
Academics.hours: See the Writing Center booking page for current hours
next_steps: Book an in-person or online consultation.
Bring your assignment prompt and current draft.
Plan to revise after the session; consultants help you edit rather than editing for you.

Academics.name: UTA Libraries
Academics.description: UTA Libraries provides research help, databases, peer-reviewed articles, course reserves and study space. Central Library is open late and offers 24-hour access during final exams.
Academics.hours: Spring 2026: Mon–Fri 7:00 a.m.–2:00 a.m.; Sat–Sun 9:00 a.m.–midnight (24 hours during finals)
next_steps: Search the library catalog and databases from libraries.uta.edu.
Use the 24/7 Ask Us chat for research help.
Reserve a study room for group work.

Academics.name: Registrar
Academics.description: The Office of the Registrar maintains enrollment and academic records: registration, enrollment verification, change of major records, name changes, the academic calendar and FERPA.
next_steps: Use MyMav for registration and to print an enrollment verification.
Email records@uta.edu for record requests not available online.
Check the academic calendar for add/drop and withdrawal deadlines.

Academics.name: Transcript Requests
Academics.description: Official UTA transcripts are ordered through the Office of the Registrar; electronic PDF transcripts can be sent directly to another school or employer.
next_steps: Order an official transcript online and choose electronic PDF delivery.
Enter the recipient's email or mailing address carefully.
Clear any holds on your account, which can block transcript release.

Academics.name: Graduation Information
Academics.description: The Registrar's graduation team handles graduation applications, degree conferral and diploma questions; commencement details are posted each term.
next_steps: Apply to graduate in MyMav by the term deadline.
Confirm your degree audit shows all requirements complete.
Email gradteam@uta.edu with diploma or conferral questions.

Academics.name: TRIO Student Support Services
Academics.description: TRIO SSS provides academic coaching, mentoring and graduation planning for eligible first-generation, low-income students and students with disabilities.
Academics.hours: See the official page for current hours
next_steps: Check TRIO eligibility requirements.
Submit the TRIO SSS application.
Meet a TRIO coach in Ransom Hall 206.

Academics.name: Undergraduate Research
Academics.description: The Office of Undergraduate Research connects students with faculty research, funded programs such as UROP, UGRAP and McNair Scholars, and the annual poster showcase.
next_steps: Browse undergraduate research programs and deadlines.
Email faculty whose work interests you, attaching a short resume.
Present your work at the undergraduate research showcase.

Academics.name: Graduate School
Academics.description: The Graduate School oversees graduate admissions policy, thesis and dissertation submission, formatting rules and graduate student support for master's and doctoral students.
Academics.hours: See the official page for current hours
next_steps: Review thesis and dissertation formatting and submission deadlines.
Coordinate deadlines with your graduate advisor.
Call the Graduate School for policy questions.

Academics.name: Supplemental Instruction
Academics.description: Supplemental Instruction (SI) offers free, peer-led group review sessions attached to historically difficult courses, run through the Academic Success Center's Academic Support Programs.
Academics.hours: Session times are posted for each supported course
next_steps: Check whether your course has an SI leader this term.
Attend sessions weekly, not just before exams.
Bring your notes and questions from lecture.

Academics.name: Math Support
Academics.description: The Math Clinic offers free drop-in help for algebra, precalculus, calculus and other lower-level mathematics courses.
Academics.hours: See the Math Clinic page for the current schedule
next_steps: Drop in to Pickard Hall 325 during clinic hours.
Bring your textbook, notes and the problems you are stuck on.
Combine clinic visits with your instructor's office hours.

Health & wellbeing.name: Health Services
Health & wellbeing.description: UTA Health Services provides appointment-based medical care for students, plus an on-site pharmacy, immunization clinic and psychiatry services.
next_steps: Call 817-272-2771 or use the MavCare portal to book an appointment.
Bring your Mav ID and insurance card.
For a life-threatening emergency call 911.

Health & wellbeing.name: Counseling & Psychological Services
Health & wellbeing.description: CAPS offers free, confidential counseling, crisis support and psychiatry referrals for stress, anxiety, depression and relationships. MAVS TALK is a 24-hour crisis line.
Health & wellbeing.location: Ransom Hall, Room 303 and Maverick Activities Center, Room 212
Health & wellbeing.hours: Mon–Fri, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; MAVS TALK crisis line 24/7
next_steps: Call 817-272-3671 to schedule a counseling appointment.
If you are in crisis, call MAVS TALK at 817-272-8255 at any time.
Use the MavCare portal for confidential messages; email is not confidential.

Health & wellbeing.name: Student Access & Resource Center
Health & wellbeing.description: The SAR Center determines eligibility for disability accommodations such as testing accommodations, extended time and note-taking, and manages accommodation requests each semester through the AIM portal.
next_steps: Follow the 'How to Request Services' steps and submit documentation.
Meet with SAR Center staff to confirm eligibility.
Request accommodation letters each semester in the AIM portal.

Health & wellbeing.name: Maverick Pantry
Health & wellbeing.description: The Maverick Pantry provides free food, toiletries and school supplies to UTA students, faculty and staff by appointment. Bring your Mav ID and reusable bags.
Health & wellbeing.hours: Spring 2026: Tue–Wed 9 a.m.–3 p.m.; Thu 12–6 p.m.; Fri 9 a.m.–12 p.m. (hours change each term)
Health & wellbeing.contact: Booking link and updates on the official page and @UTAMaverickPantry
next_steps: Book a shopping appointment through the pantry's booking link.
Bring your Mav ID and your own reusable bags.
Check current hours before you go; they change between semesters.

Health & wellbeing.name: Campus Recreation
Health & wellbeing.description: Campus Recreation runs the Maverick Activities Center (MAC) with fitness facilities, group exercise, intramural sports and sport clubs for students.
Health & wellbeing.location: Maverick Activities Center, 500 W. Nedderman Dr.
next_steps: Bring your Mav ID to enter the MAC.
Sign up for intramural teams through Campus Recreation.
Check posted hours, which change for special events.

Health & wellbeing.name: Health Insurance Information
Health & wellbeing.description: International students are enrolled in the university Academic Health Plan (AHP) unless they qualify for and submit a waiver each semester; domestic students can ask Health Services about coverage and billing insurance.
Health & wellbeing.location: Office of International Education (waivers) · Health Services (coverage questions)
Health & wellbeing.hours: Waivers due each semester by the posted deadline
next_steps: Watch your UTA email for the AHP eligibility notice.
Submit the waiver with your insurance card and benefits summary before the deadline.
Contact OIE if insurance charges remain after an approved waiver.

Health & wellbeing.name: Relationship Violence & Sexual Assault Prevention
Health & wellbeing.description: RVSP provides confidential advocacy and support for survivors of sexual assault, dating and domestic violence and stalking, plus prevention education. Walk-ins are welcome.
Health & wellbeing.contact: Confidential contact details on the official RVSP page · Emergency 911 or UTA Police 817-272-3003
next_steps: If you are in immediate danger, call 911.
Walk in to Ransom Hall 301 to talk confidentially with an advocate.
Ask about reporting options; you decide whether to report.

Health & wellbeing.name: Student Outreach & Support
Health & wellbeing.description: The Dean of Students CARE Team is a confidential network that helps students in distress and accepts referrals from anyone worried about a student. The office also reviews medical and compassionate withdrawals.
Health & wellbeing.location: Continuing Education and Workforce Development Building, 140 W Mitchell St, Suite D100
next_steps: Submit a CARE referral for yourself or a student you are worried about.
Contact the Dean of Students office to talk through options.
In an emergency call 911 or UTA Police at 817-272-3003.

International.name: International Student & Scholar Services
International.description: The Office of International Education (OIE) advises F-1 and J-1 students on immigration status, I-20 and DS-2019 documents, travel endorsements, SEVIS and maintaining status.
International.hours: Office Mon–Fri, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; advising appointments posted weekly
next_steps: Book an in-person, phone or Teams advising appointment with OIE.
Request a travel endorsement well before you leave the U.S.
Keep your I-20, passport and visa valid and your address updated.

International.name: International Employment Guidance
International.description: OIE advisors explain work authorization for F-1 and J-1 students, including on-campus employment limits, Curricular Practical Training (CPT) and Optional Practical Training (OPT).
next_steps: Review OIE's employment information and forms.
Book an advising appointment before applying for CPT or OPT.
Do not begin work until your authorization is approved.

International.name: Study Abroad
International.description: UTA Study Abroad helps students choose exchange, faculty-led and affiliate programs overseas, plan credit transfer and apply for funding.
next_steps: Attend a study abroad information session or advising.
Compare programs and confirm credit transfer with your academic advisor.
Apply for study abroad scholarships early.

International.name: International Orientation
International.description: New international students complete New Maverick Orientation with international sessions covering immigration check-in, advising and arrival logistics.
International.location: Orientation Office, CEWD Building, 140 W Mitchell St, Suite D100
next_steps: Register for an international orientation session.
Complete your immigration check-in with OIE after arrival.
Attend international advising during orientation to register for classes.

International.name: English Language Resources
International.description: The English Language Institute (ELI) offers intensive English programs to improve academic reading, writing, listening and speaking for non-native speakers.
International.location: University Hall, Room 502, 601 S. Nedderman Dr.
International.hours: Mon–Wed 1–5 p.m.; Thu 2–5 p.m.; Fri 1–3:30 p.m.
next_steps: Review ELI program levels and session dates.
Apply through ELI admissions.
Pair ELI with Writing Center visits for academic writing.

Technology.name: OIT Help Desk
Technology.description: The OIT Service Desk helps with NetID and password resets, MFA, campus Wi-Fi, email and university software. Get help by phone, chat or a self-service ticket.
Technology.location: Online and by phone (IT Service Desk)
Technology.hours: See the OIT page for current support hours
next_steps: Try the self-service password reset first.
Call the IT Service Desk at 817-272-2208 or start a chat.
Submit a ticket at uta.service-now.com/selfservice if the problem continues.

Technology.name: Canvas Support
Technology.description: Canvas Level 1 support helps students with Canvas log-ins, missing courses, assignment submissions and quizzes, around the clock by phone, chat or web ticket.
next_steps: Open Help in Canvas and start a chat with Canvas Support.
Call 1-855-597-3403 at any time.
Tell your instructor if a deadline was affected by a technical problem.

Technology.name: Student Software
Technology.description: OIT provides free or discounted software for students, including Microsoft 365, Adobe Creative Cloud and Express, MyApps and Kivuto academic software.
next_steps: Sign in to Microsoft 365 with your UTA account to install Office.
Request Adobe Creative Cloud through the OIT software page.
Use MyApps for course software that runs in the browser.

Technology.name: Computer Labs
Technology.description: OIT campus computer labs provide Mac and PC workstations, printers and scanners for student use.
Technology.location: Multiple campus locations (see the OIT labs page)
next_steps: Find the nearest lab and its hours on the OIT labs page.
Log in with your NetID.
Add print credit to your account before printing.

Technology.name: Library Technology Lending
Technology.description: UTA Libraries lends technology and equipment to students for short-term use; check availability with the library before visiting.
next_steps: Ask the library (Ask Us chat) which equipment is available.
Bring your Mav ID to check out equipment.
Return items on time to avoid fines.

Campus life.name: University Housing
Campus life.description: University Housing manages residence halls and on-campus apartments, the free housing application and room assignments, awarded first come, first served.
next_steps: Submit the free housing application early (first come, first served).
Compare residence halls and apartments.
Email housing@uta.edu with assignment questions.

Campus life.name: Dining Services
Campus life.description: UTA Dining runs campus restaurants and The Commons and offers four traditional and three on-the-go meal plans for residents and commuters.
Campus life.location: University Center, Suite 150, 301 W. First Street
Campus life.hours: Varies by location; University Center open 7 a.m.–midnight Mon–Sat (Spring 2026)
next_steps: Compare traditional and on-the-go meal plans.
Purchase a plan through the dining website.
Check each location's hours before you go.

Campus life.name: Parking & Transportation
Campus life.description: Parking and Transportation Services sells parking permits through MavPark and runs the MavMover shuttle, late-night security escort and Arlington On-Demand rides.
Campus life.location: Office and Classroom Building, 710 S. Davis Dr.
next_steps: Buy or manage your permit in MavPark.
Track MavMover shuttles live at uta.tripshot.com.
Request a late-night security escort through the MavMover app.

Campus life.name: Mav Express
Campus life.description: The Mav Express Card Office issues and replaces the Mav ID card used for building access, meal plans and campus purchases. No appointment is needed.
Campus life.hours: Mon–Tue 8 a.m.–7 p.m.; Wed–Fri 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
next_steps: Visit the Mav Express office; no appointment is needed.
Bring a government-issued photo ID.
Report a lost card right away so it can be deactivated.

Campus life.name: Student Organizations
Campus life.description: The Student Organizations office supports registered student organizations, helps students join clubs and guides officers through registering a new organization.
next_steps: Browse registered organizations from the Student Organizations page.
Attend the involvement fair at the start of each term.
Visit UC B160 to register a new organization.

Campus life.name: New Student Orientation
Campus life.description: New Maverick Orientation prepares incoming freshmen and transfer students with advising, registration and campus resources before their first semester.
Campus life.location: CEWD Building, 140 W Mitchell St, Suite D100
next_steps: Register for an orientation session after you are admitted.
Complete pre-orientation modules.
Attend advising during orientation to register for classes.

Campus life.name: Student Governance
Campus life.description: Student Governance supports Student Government, its senate and elections, giving students a voice in university decisions.
next_steps: Review election dates and candidate requirements.
Attend a Student Government meeting.
Contact Student Governance in UC B150.

Campus life.name: Multicultural Affairs
Campus life.description: The Intercultural Student Engagement Center hosts cultural programs, heritage month events, identity-based communities and inclusion initiatives.
next_steps: Check ISEC's event calendar.
Join an identity-based student community.
Email isec@uta.edu to get involved.

Campus life.name: Parent & Family Programs
Campus life.description: Parent and Family Resources help families support their student with newsletters, family weekend and guidance on university services.
Campus life.location: CEWD Building, 140 W Mitchell St, Suite D100
next_steps: Sign up for the parent and family newsletter.
Share this directory with family members.
Email parents@uta.edu with questions.

Career & support.name: Career Development Center
Career & support.description: The Career Development Center offers career appointments, resume critiques, interview-skills programs, workshops and job and internship fairs. Appointments are booked in Handshake.
next_steps: Book a career appointment in Handshake.
Upload your resume for a critique before a career fair.
Attend an interview-skills workshop.

Career & support.name: Student Employment
Career & support.description: On-campus student jobs and part-time positions are posted in Handshake through the Career Development Center.
next_steps: Search on-campus jobs in Handshake.
Complete hiring paperwork promptly when you receive an offer.
International students: confirm on-campus work limits with OIE.

Career & support.name: Dean of Students
Career & support.description: The Dean of Students office advocates for students, takes complaints about treatment or procedures, reviews medical and compassionate withdrawals, and handles Title IX and hazing reports.
Career & support.location: CEWD Building, 140 W Mitchell St, Suite D100
next_steps: Use 'Report a Concern' to file a complaint.
Request a medical or compassionate withdrawal review if needed.
Call 817-272-7862 to speak with staff.

Career & support.name: Student Conduct
Career & support.description: The Office of Community Standards manages the student conduct process, including academic integrity cases, hearings and appeals.
Career & support.location: University Center, Lower Level, Suite B150
next_steps: Read your notice carefully and respond by the stated date.
Review the student conduct process and your rights.
Call Community Standards at 817-272-2354 with questions.

Career & support.name: University Police Resources
Career & support.description: UTA Police serve campus 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, take crime reports such as theft and provide safety services including the late-night escort.
next_steps: For emergencies call 911 or 817-272-3003.
Report non-emergency crimes such as theft at 817-272-3381.
Request a safety escort through the MavMover app at night.
